name: Virtual Memory Volume Rendering
aliases: Virtual Memory Architecture for Volume Rendering
definition: A volume rendering architecture that virtualizes 3D volumes by subdividing them into small 3D blocks (e.g., 32^3 voxels). It uses a multi-resolution page table hierarchy to map virtual addresses to physical cache blocks, allowing on-demand construction of 3D blocks from 2D input streams only when accessed during ray-casting.
summary: Virtual Memory Volume Rendering is an out-of-core architecture that enables interactive petascale microscopy exploration by using a multi-resolution page table hierarchy to map 3D blocks to a GPU cache, avoiding explicit octree traversal.
